lines: Registro: cotidiano gentil; cuidadora.
Características: acolhe sem pressionar ("Apenas relaxe..."); curiosa mas paciente; calor humano.
Red flags: soar fria, clínica ou impaciente; formalidade excessiva.
Haku (protagonista, narração 1ª pessoa) — `voice_criticality: high`. Predomina nas 2 cenas:
Registro: enigmático, profético, frio.
Características: sentenças curtas e definitivas; duplo sentido ("um mundo totalmente novo te espera"); ambiguidade ameaçadora.
Red flags: soar caloroso/paternal; resolver a ambiguidade (a fala deve permanecer dúbia).
Registro: erudito cômico, pomposo e arcaico; bajulador do Ukon; alívio cômico.
Características: fala arcaica/empolada (equivalente a "vós/peço-vos/meus olhos não me enganam") + gag de cicio (s→sh, ex.: "SHEEKETH"/"shir"); melodramático; gruda no Haku como "benfeitor".
Red flags: perder o arcaísmo ou o cicio (são a piada); soar moderno/neutro; explicar a comédia. Manter o contraste entre a pompa do vocabulário e a fragilidade do personagem.
Nosuri — `voice_criticality: medium`. Fora-da-lei atrevida e malandra; "aliada da justiça" irônica; oportunista. Registro coloquial/esperto.

Oshtor — `voice_criticality: high`. = Ukon até 13_08 (ver spoiler_ledger). Registro formal, nobre, comedido; General da Direita. Antes do reveal, traduzir como o mercenário "Ukon" (espirituoso, informal) — NÃO antecipar a pompa de general
Ougi — `voice_criticality: low`. Irmão da Nosuri; pragmático, parceria com a irmã.
Registro: confuso, desorientado, semi-consciente.
Características: frases quebradas por reticências; perguntas curtas ("Quem... é você...?"); pouca pontuação forte.
Red flags: falas fluentes/articuladas demais; perder o tom de torpor; pontuação "limpa" que apaga a fragmentação.
Rulutieh — `voice_criticality: medium`. Princesa tímida e gentil; hesitante (gagueja quando nervosa: "P-Princesa..."), educada, se anima ao falar de arte/BL. Não soar arrogante apesar de princesa.
Registro: guerreiro carismático, espirituoso, caloroso e informal; líder nato que trata Haku como um irmão mais novo.
Características: desembaraçado, brincalhão, generoso; fala direta e cativante; autoridade leve (lidera a Coorte) sem arrogância.
Red flags: soar rígido/formal/militar demais (a graça é justamente o contraste com a patente); frieza. SPOILER: não deixar a tradução insinuar a identidade verdadeira — no cap.12 ele é só "Ukon".

decisions.title: Opcode de RÓTULO DE FALANTE `53 00` + reconcile de speaker (data-driven)
decisions.summary: **Problema:** in-game, o rótulo de falante aparecia em **inglês** ("Girl") mesmo com a tradução ("Garota") aprovada e gravada. RE: o nome do falante usa um **2º opcode de ponteiro, `53 00`** (mesmo formato file-relativo do `50 00` de diálogo), que o conector ignorava. Resultado: "Girl"→"Garota"

decisions.title: Gate de charset pt-BR — método e veredito
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: likely` e exigir confirmação in-game antes de produção. **Alternativas consideradas:** - Confirmar por presença no texto-fonte — **insuficiente**: o fonte é inglês e quase não usa acentos (só `õ` e `À` aparecem em texto real).

decisions.title: Anomalia 0x33f9 — texto PT/EN corrompido na fonte
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar a linha `0x33f9` como anomalia de fonte (não traduzir em cima do lixo; tratar como linha de sistema reescrita). **Razão:** A string original já vem misturada PT/EN e truncada ("...SISTEMAS AM . RESTARTING...") no próprio jogo. Não é erro de extração. O conector deve sinali

decisions.title: Charset — transliteração na gravação (gate FALHOU)
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Marcar `target_charset_supported: false` e **transliterar** (acento → ASCII) na gravação do binário. A tradução canônica (`approved_translations.csv`, `translation_plan.json`) **mantém os acentos** (correta para QA/revisão); apenas os bytes escritos no jogo são dobrados para ASCI

Novos termos canônicos: **Kuon** (nome revelado em 0x108db), **Haku** (nome dado ao protagonista em 0x12668 — reveal agora **dentro do corpus**), **Tatari** (criatura imortal), **aperyu** (vestimenta), **

decisions.title: CORREÇÃO CRÍTICA — ponteiros são FILE-RELATIVOS, não absolutos
decisions.summary: **Decisão tomada:** Ao investigar o "opcode de início de bloco", descobri que **`50 00`+uint32 é um offset RELATIVO ao início do arquivo (Pack)**, não absoluto. Endereço da string = `file_start_do_site + uint32`. Prova: dos ~47k sites, **42.101** só apontam para string como file-relativos vs **63**

lines.source: *Yawn*... Mmf.
I try to suppress the large yawn, but it will\n
not be denied.
Hmhm. That was quite the yawn.
Yeah, guess I'm still a little sleepy.
I glance up. Little by little, the eastern sky\n
is getting brighter.
Usually I'd be snoring in bed at this hour.
This isn't the first time I've gone with Kuon\n
to morning market, but I could still use a nap...
Haku?
Mm?
Thanks for coming.
...Sure, no problem.
I hear a lot of shouting around the area...\n
Merchants trying to get the attention of\n
potential customers.
I peer around. I'm actually kind of impressed\n
by how many people are so functional this early.
...Seems more lively than usual today, huh?
Kuon gives a small nod in response, glancing\n
around herself.
You're right. There's rumors that there's going\n
to be a war... Maybe that's why?
A war?
I heard that Uzurusha in the west is invading\n
Yamato. They've already taken a bordering\n
country.
Yamato must be gathering their troops to fight\n
off the invaders.
What!? That's the first I've heard of it. Isn't\n
it pretty bad if they already took someone else\n
down?
Then again, I don't see a single worried face\n
out here.
In fact, there's almost a sense of excitement.\n
Like there's going to be a festival or\n
something.
I imagine that not a single citizen thinks\n
there's a chance Yamato could lose this war.
Kuon probably guessed my question from my\n
expression. She continues on.
It just goes to show how much faith the people\n
of this country have in the Mikado.
Faith in the Mikado, huh...?
The unified country of Yamato, made up of smaller\n provinces. And the owlo that rules over them...
That old geezer's... No, never mind. Didn't\n
see anything, don't KNOW anything.
That should do it. We've gotten everything on the\n
list, so we can head home now.
We need to get this to Rulutieh before everyone\n
wakes up, or breakfast will be late.
Right you are.
Ohhh... Hmmm...
What to do? I can't just ignore a direct order\n
from Papa...
And it DOES sound like a bash... but I definitely\n
don't want all those sweaty boys with me...
After we finish breakfast, Atuy sits there with\n
a letter in hand, looking deeply pensive.
Atuy? Is something wrong?
It's pretty rare to see you so deep in thought\n
like this.
Well, I got a letter from Papa today, and...\n
oh, it's a touch complicated.
Is it something serious? You don't look too\n
happy about whatever it says.
Well, you see--Oh!
Just as Atuy is about to explain, she claps her\n
hands together, as if inspiration's struck.
I know. Are you two busy at all right now?
Hm?
No. There aren't any pressing matters we need\n
to take care of right now.
Really?
Well there's nothing urgent, but that doesn't\n
mean we're completely free...
Well, in that case, could you come with me\n
for a bit? There's somewhere I'd like to go.
Atuy smiles cheerfully...
Hah! What a shame for you, Kuon. It seems\n
victory is mine.
We'll see about that.
Well, I hope for your sake you don't cry when\n
you lose! Hyah!
Five, huh... One, two, three... Now, take this\n
piece... or move two more to take the other...?
...I'll take this one!
So sorry, but that was a mistake. The trap is\n
sprung. What you really should've watched \n
out for is this!
Im... possible!
All right... my turn now.
Five and three, that makes eight... So I take\n
this piece at four...
Grrrrr...
And I think that's game. You lose double points.
W-Wait! M-My hand slipped back there! What I\n
really wanted was THAT piece!
A good woman would never go back on her\n
word, I'd think?
Arrrgh! How!? How could I have lost like this!?
So many wins in a row. Most impressive,\n
dear sister.
I didn't know you were so skilled in these games,\n
Miss Kuon...
My mothers were all fond of games like these.\n
I just naturally got better from playing with\n
them.
...Hmhmhm. I would expect no less from a worthy\n
rival like yourself. It's no fun without a\n
challenge.
But now... you have awakened the BEAST WITHIN.
Looks like it's time I show you what happens\n
when I get serious...
I hear the girls happily chatting behind me.
Sounds like they're having fun back there...
With reins in hand, keeping an eye on the steeds\n
moving us forward, I let out a small sigh.
We're in the mountains north of the imperial\n
capital. A dense forest covers the mountainside.
In the carriage behind us, Ougi, Kiwru, and\n
Cocopo follow along.
And where the hell did they get this carriage\n
from...?
The carriage Kuon turned up with had all kinds\n
of travel supplies. We're fine, even in the\n
mountains.
Not only did it have enough food and clothes,\n
it included beds, and even a simple cooking\n
stove.
It also had all the amenities for bathing...\n
It seems designed for long-term traveling in\n
comfort.
Even had a couple games packed in for road\n
entertainment. Swanky.
That's all fine. It's all fine, but...
...We've clearly been traveling for longer than\n
"a bit." It's been quite a while now.
That's right... It's been about three days\n
since we set out.
This is becoming more of a road trip than\n
anything else.
I think we might be pretty close to the\n
country's border now.
Danger. Evasive maneuvers recommended.
Master, there appears to be a large tree root\n
protruding from the ground in front of us.
Whoa.
I quickly shift the reins, guiding our path\n
around them.
Thanks, you two.
I glance both right and left to acknowledge\n
each of the twins.
The two of them aren't joining in with the\n
others' games, and they sit next to me as\n
usual.
Aren't you guys going to play a couple rounds\n
with them?
The two of them shake their heads instantly at\n
my question; no deliberation required.
We stay with you, Master.
The only place we belong is at your side,\n
Master.
O-OK, I get it. But could you two quit leaning\n
on me?
All that warmth and softness is getting...\n
distracting...
Hey there, love!
Gah!?
And now Atuy's jumped on me from behind.
Get off. You're heavy.
Hee hee, you shouldn't ever joke about something\n
like that to a girl, you know...
*Badump*...
I don't know why, but Atuy's smile sends a\n
shiver down my spine.
Y-Yeah, guess you're right.
I'm glad you understand. If you actually meant\n
it, well, I might have to start a teensy little\n
war.
R-Right...
Hmm, we should be pretty close now... 'Scuse\n
me, love.
Atuy leans forward on me to get a look around.\n
And, of course, pressing on the back of my\n
head...
What are you--
Hmmm, still might be a little ways off...
Hey, Atuy. Do you mind telling me where exactly\n
we're going?
What do you mean?
Don't play dumb with me. This has gone way past\n
"coming with you for a bit."
I thought you just wanted a little sightseeing\n
trip, but we've gone way too far out now.\n
Where are we even going?
Oh, you needn't worry. I already got Oshtor's\n
permission and everything!
What? What do you--
...Oh! I think I see it now.
I wonder where Atuy is taking us.
We're quite far from the capital. And all this\n
ominous talk of war coming... I wonder if\n
it's safe.
I'm certain there is little cause for worry.\n
Our compatriots certainly seem cheerful enough.
Ougi gestures towards the carriage in front with\n
a placid smile.
Through the window of the car, they can see\n
the girls playing games.
They've switched from sugoroku to shogi, but\n
they still look to be having fun together.
That would be... check.
What!? N-No, what I MEANT to do was this!
As you please. Then I will take your hisha\n
instead.
Wha--!?
I am glad indeed to see my dear sister enjoying\n
herself.
A life with more subordinates than friends has\n
left her quite lonely. I much prefer to see her\n
smile so.
It would appear that the others' circumstances\n
are not dissimilar... Birds of a feather, as\n
they say.
Ougi. Why do I get the feeling you're insulting--\n
Huh?
A shadow falls over Kiwru's expression.
Ougi, is that...?
Yes. Without a doubt...
We finally get out of the forest, and proceed\n
into an open field.
*Whistle*
Whoa there.
...Huh?
I'm not sure what just happened.
I thought I saw something fly towards me\n
really fast.
Then Atuy's hand appeared, and... I see an arrow\n
caught between her fingers, still vibrating with\n
force.
Ahahaha! Looks like they've started without us.
I finally realize. A stray arrow had almost\n
pierced my head, and Atuy somehow caught it\n
in time.
Wh-Wh... What in the...
My near-death reaction finally kicks in, and\n
a cold sweat breaks out all over me.
We can hear yelling in the distance, and the\n
sound of metal clashing against metal.
The infrequent crackling of a fire, and the\n
scent of burnt flesh.
Well, well, well...
..."Dear Grandfather,
The moment I was free from the forest...\n
I suddenly found myself on a battlefield."
What the hell is going on here!? What is this!?\n
What the hell IS this!? Where the hell are we!?
Oh, it's just as it looks, love. A lovely little\n
playground.
A playground!? This!?
Don't you play dumb with me!
I heard there was a war going on at the borders,\n
but...
Anyways, let's get out of here before we're\n
caught in even more trouble.
Why?
What do you mean, "why?"...
We came all the way here to have some fun!\n
It'd be a bit of a waste if we turn around now.
For this...? Wait... Did you know that the war\n
was going on here?
More than that. I came to join the war in Papa's\n
stead. He's too busy to come himself, so he\n
asked me.
Wait a minute. That letter...
I was rather looking forward to it, but he\n
demanded I take some of his men along. And\n
they're a bit too sweaty.
Just imagine it. A glistening mob of muscle-bound\n
lunks chasing after me yelling "Milady, milady!"
That all sounds a bit nasty to me, so I decided\n
to invite you loves along for some fun instead.
Fun? This...?
I asked Oshtor, and he said he didn't mind.\n
He said if I'm having a party, then go wild!
Party!? He just wanted us to be his advance\n
party!
Look, to you this may be all fun and games,\n
but this is war.
You shouldn't be dragging us all into this.
I... shouldn't?
Of course you aren't! You can't be dragging your\n
friends onto a battlefield. That's ridiculous.
But... I just wanted to have fun... with\n
everybody...
Oh, I guess we've arrived. Things look pretty\n
hectic out there.
Just as my dear brother was saying, it seems\n
the war has indeed escalated.
Whuh?
Nosuri, Ougi, can I ask you for some\n
reconnaissance? I'd like to know where the\n
enemy's stationed.
Leave it to us. And let me remind you: I demand\n
a rematch after this!
Rulutieh, Nekone, I want you two to scope out\n
the area. We need to get a feel for the terrain.
Yes.
Understood. Let's go, Cocopo.
How are they acting so calmly...? Wait a\n
minute. Did they know about this...?
H-Hey, Kuon. Was all this... an inconvenience\n
for you?
Should I have... not invited my friends here?
Atuy...
I don't think that's true. I've never been\n
invited out by a friend like this. It made\n
me happy.
Kuon...
Kuon, you don't seem too fazed by all this.\n
Did you know all along?
What?
Wait, Haku, are you telling me you DIDN'T know?\n
I thought you knew from the beginning.
How was I supposed to know this from the\n
beginning?
Well, it was pretty apparent what her father's\n
letter would be about.
Atuy is royalty, so it makes sense that she'd\n
represent her father and lead soldiers against\n
the invasion.
My dear brother has also departed for the\n
battlefield with his troops.
Wait, did you two know about this as well?
Oh... OK...
Did Nosuri know about this too?
Indubitably. We were the ones who gathered the\n
supplies for the trip.
Yes, I was aware of it.
What about Rulutieh?
Um... I was...
Rulutieh's also royalty. I imagine she's in the\n
same position as Atuy. She also knew from the\n
start.
Um, I'm sorry...
What about you, Kiwru? You knew about this too?
U-Um... O-Of course I knew about it! What do\n
you take me for?
